wikiGoal:
# Benchmark documentation brief

Create a source-grounded wiki for engineers who must understand, operate, debug, and safely change this repository.

- Explain the architecture, ownership boundaries, core data/control flows, persistence, external integrations, configuration, and failure handling.
- Include a practical quickstart and focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks.
- Treat source code and tests as authoritative. Cite concrete source evidence for every non-obvious technical claim.
- State uncertainty when the repository does not establish a fact. Do not invent runtime behavior, guarantees, or deployment details.
- Prefer a coherent, non-overlapping taxonomy over exhaustive file-by-file narration.

pages.title: Architecture: crates, the decision core, and the effect-execution loop
pages.purpose: System overview: the three-crate workspace, the logic/executor ownership boundary, the serial actor that feeds Events to on_event and executes returned Effects, asyncrt facade, and build/toolchain shape.
instructions: Cite concrete spans for on_event, Event/Effect, and the actor mailbox/versioned completion pattern.
Explain why the split exists (deterministic simulation, model checking) and how adapters must never mutate State directly.
Mention build profiles (release/lab), jemalloc, and the celld_internal_tests cfg with env-include test modules.

pages.title: Cell lifecycle: phases, activation, and eviction
pages.purpose: The cell state machine in the decision core: Phase ladder from Inactive through cold activation to Resident/Dormant/hibernated, admission permits, alarms, eviction and shedding order, and generation swaps.
instructions: Cross-reference coordination (ownership acquire/claim) and durability (output gate) instead of re-explaining them.
Ground every phase transition claim in crates/logic/lib.rs and the module files; describe invariants enforced by State::validate.
Include capacity/activation/eviction permit ceilings from Config and where they come from in the environment.

pages.title: Coordination: bucket records, ownership, leases, and fencing
pages.purpose: Ownership and fencing: bucket layout of authority objects, conditional-write acquisition, node leases and renewal, self-fencing, the takeover interlock, ambiguous-CAS reconciliation, wake entries, and dead-node reconciliation.
instructions: Cite logic modules (Claim/RestoreSpec, MAX_ACQUIRE_RECONCILES) and celld adapters (ownership_store, bucket, fleet) for the split between decision and I/O.
Cover the probe command and startup test, and the reserved bucket prefixes.
State the bucket's required properties and what happens when they are violated (two-writer risk).

pages.title: Durability and replication: output gate, SQLite, LTX, and the node log
pages.purpose: Durability data path: the output gate (RPO=0 acknowledgement rule), per-cell SQLite storage, LTX segment capture and bucket replication via celld-ltx, the fleet node-log ensemble with followers and hedging, and restore.
instructions: Cite crates/logic/output_gate.rs and replication code spans, not just docs.
Cover compaction levels and bundles from crates/ltx plus the node-side adapters.
Describe the data path from a committed SQLite write through capture to bucket objects, and which parts are byte-compatible with the documented LTX/Litestream lineage.
State the RPO=0 acknowledgement rule as code, not marketing: gate opens only on proof; failure returns to Resident.

pages.title: The JavaScript runtime: V8, isolates, and Workers APIs
pages.purpose: The V8 host: one isolate per cell, bootstrap prelude/harness caching, ES module resolution and builtins, isolate pooling, Worker/DO dispatch, streams, WebSockets, crypto, Node compat, and WebAssembly.
instructions: Explain what a node actually runs (Wrangler bundles via esbuild output) and how bindings are wired from deployment metadata.
Note the V8 heap limit behavior and hibernatable WebSocket acceptance rules with code citations.
The Cloudflare-compat page owns the supported/gap matrix; here cover the engine mechanics and where a JS API is implemented (Rust op vs JS builtin).

pages.title: Routing and the peer network
pages.purpose: Request routing and the peer network: the two HTTP listeners, public Worker ingress, cell fetch/RPC/WebSocket proxying, the /peer/tunnel establishment with fleet HMAC, peer probes, capacity handoff hints, and outbound WebSockets.
instructions: Cite routing re-send policy, replay protection retention, and the unauthenticated operator routes list from code.
Cover the request path: public ingress → routing table → local resident vs remote owner, including the tunneled hop and its version refusal.
Distinguish the node log's use of the peer transport from cell-call use of the tunnel.

pages.title: Deployments: bundling, publication, and generation adoption
pages.purpose: Application deployment and release adoption: celld deploy building a Wrangler project, the deployment objects and protocol types written to the bucket, the deploy pointer polling, in-place generation adoption and DO swap, static assets, and the celld dev local loop.
instructions: Generation adoption mechanics are the interesting part: safe-point detection and forced swap at CELLD_DEPLOY_MAX_AGE_S.
Ground the deploy publication format in protocol.rs type names and paths.
Mention the managed control plane (celld connect) as a distinct onboarding path verified in control_plane.rs.
celld dev belongs here: local_store backend, watcher rules, and what is retained across restarts.

pages.title: Change guides: common maintenance tasks
pages.purpose: Focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks: adding a CELLD_* env option, adding or changing an Event/Effect and its executor handling, adding a JS builtin/op, changing the peer or bucket protocol surface, and adding an operator CLI subcommand.
instructions: For each task include what tests exist to prove the change and what documentation (docs/, help text) must move with it.
Give step-by-step change recipes with exact anchor files for each task.
Keep guidance grounded: prefer 'follow the existing pattern in file X' over invented conventions.

pages.title: Testing and verification strategy
pages.purpose: How correctness is earned and how to run checks in this repo: the four verification layers (differential conformance, TLA+ models, deterministic simulation of the logic core, live-fleet fault injection) and the cfg(celld_internal_tests) build seam.
instructions: Be honest about this checkout: the conformance test bodies are env-var-gated includes whose corpora live outside the workspace (see lib.rs cfg blocks); `cargo test` in a plain checkout runs what the gate exposes.
Do not describe CI or lab automation beyond what workflows and docs show.
Document clippy.toml disallowed patterns as mechanical enforcement of the actor boundary.

pages.title: Built-in services: KV, D1, Queues, Workflows, cron, and R2
pages.purpose: Cloudflare-compatible services implemented as reserved cells: KV, D1, Queues, Workflows, cron triggers, alarms, and R2 on the fleet bucket; plus the operator CLI paths that reach them.
instructions: Document the 'reserved cell with __ prefix' pattern and the HMAC /runtime route the CLIs use.
Ground each service in its logic module and js/cli adapter, not only docs.
Note limits (e.g. KV large-value bucket requirement, queue retention) with code or doc citations; the compat page owns the full gap matrix.

pages.title: Cloudflare compatibility surface
pages.purpose: The Cloudflare compatibility contract: what celld accepts from Wrangler configuration, the supported service and runtime API matrix, compatibility flags, and known silent gaps.
instructions: Cross-check the honored compatibility flags against crates/celld/lib.rs worker_compat.
State the repo rule that an unsupported feature without an error is a defect, and list the known silent gaps the doc names.
The table itself lives in the doc; cite it as the maintained matrix rather than restating every row.

pages.title: Object storage providers and credentials
pages.purpose: Object storage integration: the single bucket client, the three provider dialects (s3://, gs://, az://) and their conditional-write semantics, credential chains and validation, the storage probe, and the local dev store.
instructions: Cover the conditional-write dialect differences (etag vs generation) and error classification (clean reject vs ambiguous).
Credential family rules and rejections are operational safety: cite startup validation code.
Qualify store status exactly as docs/guarantees.md does; do not imply unqualified stores work.
local_store belongs here as the dev-only backend with SQLite transactionality.

pages.title: Configuration: flags, environment, and defaults
pages.purpose: Configuration surface: CLI actions and flags, the CELLD_* environment variables and their strict parsing, listener addresses, and defaults an operator must know.
instructions: Cover listener binding rules (advertise requires explicit internal listener, public-IP refusal without the unsafe opt-in).
Do not enumerate every CELLD_ var; organize by function and point to `celld -h` for the complete list.
Explain strict parsing consequences (invalid value stops startup) with code evidence.

pages.title: Node lifecycle: startup, shutdown, and pressure
pages.purpose: Running a node: startup validation, graceful shutdown and handoff pacing, drain tokens, readiness gating for rollouts, memory-pressure shedding, and V8 heap limits.
instructions: Cover startup ordering (listeners bound before storage/V8 work), the initial storage probe, and first-readiness fleet gate.
Graceful shutdown: drain batches, snapshots, releases, successor acks, drain token, deadlines; cite drain.rs/drain_token.rs.
Memory pressure: threshold vs absolute cap, cgroup working set math, shed walk-down and hysteresis, cite memory.rs/pressure.rs.
Upgrade notes are version-specific in docs/README.md; cite them as documented exceptions, and state that current-version upgrade procedure beyond docs claims is not established in the repo.

pages.title: Observability: /state, diagnose, and telemetry
pages.purpose: Observability: the /state operator snapshot, celld diagnose, node logging and the fleet log pipeline, and the telemetry subsystem (Parquet-to-bucket and OTLP sinks, DuckDB querying).
instructions: Cite the /state snapshot content in main.rs and the phase-name stability comment in logic.
Note the schema is v0-unstable as stated in the doc.
Telemetry config table belongs in docs; here explain the mechanics: sink selection at init, flush triggers, retention.

pages.title: Security boundaries and threats
pages.purpose: Security model and operator duties: the trusted-private-network boundary, listener protection, fleet HMAC and replay protection, unauthenticated operator routes, forwarded headers, body limits, and the bucket as root of trust.
instructions: Cover peer_auth request signing and the tunnel establishment asymmetry (establishment signed, inner calls not).
Include forwarded-header and Host policy defaults from code.
Keep bucket-as-root-of-trust prominent; alpha status is a documented fact.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical getting-started path: install, run an example locally with celld dev, deploy to a bucket, start nodes, and basic build commands for contributors.
instructions: Base the install/dev/deploy walkthrough on README.md and docs/README.md, but verify flags and defaults against crates/celld/main/cli.rs and crates/celld/env_vars.rs.
End with where an engineer should go next in this wiki.
Use the examples/ README list to point at a runnable project; do not invent commands not present in the repo.
